query: What signals are linked to longer resolution duration values?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Incident type (database, email, vpn, network) is known at intake and plausibly drives how long resolution takes; sits outside the duration and carries genuine predictive signal.

per_column.name: incident_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom class (connectivity_failure, access_denied, outage) is observable early and different symptoms have systematically different fix times; legitimate predictor, no leakage.

per_column.name: affected_system_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (single_user vs system_wide/service_wide) is knowable at diagnosis and strongly plausibly correlates with resolution effort/duration; not a restatement of the outcome.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether the assignee matches the appropriate resolver group is plausibly predictive of routing efficiency and thus duration. Mildly ambiguous timing, but generally determinable at assignment, so treat as a weak-to-moderate predictor rather than leakage.

per_column.name: open_hour_band
per_column.rationale: The time band an incident is opened (after_hours, overnight, business_hours) is known at intake and plausibly affects staffing availability and hence resolution time; clean predictor derived from opened_at.

per_column.name: opened_day_of_week
per_column.rationale: Weekday vs weekend at open time affects staffing and SLA clocks; known at intake, plausible predictive signal, no leakage.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Specific agent handling the ticket plausibly carries signal about resolution speed (experience/workload); known during handling and outside the duration value itself.

per_column.name: caller_type
per_column.rationale: Caller category (named_user vs itil_user) is known at intake and may correlate with issue complexity and prioritization, plausibly predictive of duration.

judge.rationale: All eight added columns are variables that lie outside the resolution-duration focus, are knowable at or before resolution (no post-outcome leakage), and each plausibly carries signal about how long resolution takes. The set spans complementary dimensions -- issue type/symptom/scope, temporal open-time features, routing/agent, and caller type -- giving a model meaningful additional leverage beyond the raw columns. Utility is high but not maximal because several features (open_hour_band, opened_day_of_week) are derivable from existing opened_at and thus add limited fresh information, and resolver_match/agent effects may be partly collinear with existing assignment fields.
